newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujarat state wins $250-mln ADB loan.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujarat state wins $250-mln ADB loan.

text.p: India's western state of Gujarat said on Monday that it had won a $250 million loan from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to support economic reforms.

The state government said in a statement that the loan would support reforms in public finance, as well as the power, road and port sectors. It would also be used to help restructure public sector undertakings to make them more productive, it said.
Gujarat was the first state in India to receive a loan for structural reforms at the state level from any international lending agency, it said.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Gujarat chief secretary S.K. Shelat as saying the state was negotiating with the ADB for an additional $600 million in loans for power sector development and infrastructure financing.

The news agency quoted ADB director John Taylor as telling a news conference in New Delhi: "We have confidence in India's economic reform reform process and a seven percent GDP target is sustainable given its resources and capabilities."
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government has set a medium-term target of seven percent annual growth of gross domestic product.
PTI quoted Taylor as saying the multilateral lender was in talks with Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan states over similar loan packages.
PTI said the federal government would bear the entire foreign exchange risk for the 15-year loan, which carries an annual interest rate of 13 percent.
The news agency said an initial $100-million tranche of the loan had already been released, making the "effective rate of interest" about nine percent.
